notes: Grain is on only in the four "grain" stage rows (grain_defaults, grain_stock_35mm, grain_response_film, grain_color); every other row still forces it off so grain cannot add noise to a measurement of something else. gpu.js now has a real grain shader and those four rows measure it exact against ffmpeg, but only for a rendered STILL: the plate is one frame's worth, not one plate per output frame, so this says nothing about a playing or looping preview (see STAGE_NOTES.grain in gpu.js).

ffmpeg times include the HTTP round trip and the server's own decode, and the server caches by config, so a repeated config is much faster than a fresh one. The median below is over first-time renders in this sweep only.
The GPU warm number is a re-render with the source texture and every look up table already resident, which is the case while a slider moves.
